title: Interview candidate journey radio check and ops notes
content:
Purpose:
A compact operational checklist ("radio check") for the candidate journey from offer acceptance through first week handoff. Designed for small hires, contractors, and embedded rotations where we need a lean, repeatable set of actions that can be executed asynchronously across People Ops, IT, hiring manager, and the assigned buddy.

Scope: 
- Applies to US/EMEA remote hires and contractors (hybrid/local office exceptions noted per location).
- Focus on first 7 days (preboarding + week 0).
- Lightweight interview-to-onboard continuity: captures outstanding interview evidence, candidate expectations, and immediate access tasks.

How to use this doc (1-line):
- Do a radio-check 72h, 48h, and 2h before candidate's official start. Use the quick script at the bottom. Mark status in the hiring-ops Slack thread and update HR ticket.

Quick timeline (core checkpoints):
- Offer accepted -> T-minus 7 days: assign buddy & create access checklist.
- T-minus 5 days: IT provisioning request, calendar emit: "Welcome + First 1:1" to candidate + manager + buddy.
- T-minus 3 days: radio check #1 (ops): candidate able to log into SSO + email? onboarding docs sent?
- T-minus 1 day: radio check #2 (manager/buddy): agenda for day 0, quick intro notes.
- Start day, 2h pre: radio check #3 (buddy): confirm equipment, meeting links, timezone, emergency contact.
- Day 3: candidate feedback pulse + missing access escalation.
- Day 7: handoff retrospective to hiring manager and close HR ticket.

Preboarding checklist (assign owner per row):
- SSO/email created (IT) — test login (ops)
- Slack invite + timezone channel (ops)
- HR docs sent + signed (recruiter/ops)
- Payroll/KYC in progress (finance ops)
- Laptop order / shipping tracking (IT/procurement)
- VPN/VPC access request (security) — if private deployment work, escalate to infra
- Manager welcome note + role context doc (hiring manager)
- Buddy assigned + 30m intro scheduled (hiring manager)

Interview evidence and quick rubric (lightweight capture)
- Purpose: keep hiring manager and product/platform teams able to reference quick signals if we need to re-evaluate role fit during onboarding.
- Format: one-sentence signal + 1–3 line context. Add to the candidate card in Greenhouse/HRIS.

Rubric shorthand (0–4):
- 4 = Strong technical signal + culture alignment
- 3 = Meets bar, some ramp technical work expected
- 2 = Fitable with strong manager support and early paired tasks
- 1 = Borderline — escalate to hiring manager & people ops for fit discussion
- 0 = Reject/withdrawn

Example capture (paste into candidate card):
- Eng technical (pairing): 3 — completed pairing on service design, needs initial ramp on infra patterns; manager will pair week 1.
- System design: 2 — conceptually good, missed depth on error-handling; give pair assignment to surface learning.
- Behavioral: 4 — strong ownership signal, cross-team communication examples.

First 7 days - prioritized manager/buddy actions (practical):
Day 0:
- 30m welcome + role context (manager)
- 60m buddy walkthrough: repo layout, running dev env, local quickstart checklist (buddy)
- 20m SRE/infra intro if relevant (infra)
- 30m HR check-in and benefits overview (ops)

Day 1–2:
- Small dev task: get a repo clone + green test run (manager assigns)
- Pause checkpoints: daily 15m sync with buddy (first 3 days)

Day 3–7:
- Deliverable: small bugfix or doc improvement merged (measurable ramp)
- Manager triage meeting end of week: 30m (close out any interview evidence actions)

Common failure modes and remediation (ops playbook):
- Candidate can’t access SSO/email: escalate to IT triage — open IT ticket and assign ops owner.
- Laptop delayed: provide temporary loaner + document remote setup steps.
- Access gaps to private infra: temporary work shadowing with read-only tasks until approvals complete.

Asynchronous feedback template (for interviewers to complete during preboarding):
- 3-line summary of interview signal
- Rubric score (0–4)
- 1 immediate onboarding action (e.g., "pair with infra on Wed 10am")
- Add to candidate card and tag #hiring-ops in Slack with a 1-line highlight

Radio-check quick script (use verbatim in Slack/phone/email):
- 72h radio-check (ops → candidate): "Hi <Name>, this is Mariel from Redwood People Ops. Quick check — could you confirm you received the welcome packet, that your preferred email is <email>, and that you can sign into our SSO? Reply 'OK' and I'll follow up with next steps. Thanks!"
- 48h radio-check (manager/buddy → candidate): "Hi <Name>, this is <Buddy>. Quick note: we have your day 0 at <time> — I'll ping you 2h before to confirm setup. Anything you want us to prioritize?"
- 2h radio-check (buddy → candidate): "Quick ping to confirm laptop, camera, meeting link and timezone. If anything is off, reply and I'll get IT on it immediately."

Handoff close checklist (end of week 1):
- Hiring manager confirms ramp tasks assigned and merged sample work
- Ops closes HR ticket and confirms payroll/benefits onboarding completed
- Buddy hands over 1-page context doc to manager with unresolved learning items
- Candidate pulse note added to HRIS

Unresolved questions / backlog items:
- Do we need a simple read-only checklist for private-deployment hires that maps approvals to expected lead times per region? (open: HR-2035)
- Should interns/short contractors skip formal KYC for tax reasons in some markets? Follow finance guidance.

Notes, tone, and intent:
- Keep radio checks short and permissioned — candidate experience is primary.
- The doc is intentionally terse: treat as an ops play that can be copy/pasted into Slack templates and ticket comments.

Operational shortcuts and handy links: 
- Slack template: /template radio-check-72h (in #hiring-ops)
- Confluence onboarding index: https://confluence.redwood.company/display/PO/Candidate-Journey-Index
- HR ticket reference: add candidate GH id + "radio-check" tag to ticket

If you execute the three radio checks and tick every preboarding item, we reduce early fracturing (access, expectations, equipment) by ~85% (empirical, Q3 pilot).

Last edited by: Mariel Santos — notes: piloting simplified version for Q1 2026 hires; requesting feedback from hiring managers (add reactions in #hiring-ops).
